description: Use an API token with Zone Read and DNS Read. Add DNS Write for record changes and Zone Write for zone creation. Account ID is required.
name: Cloudflare

ttl.help: Automatic TTL is supported. Manual values must be between 60 and 86400 seconds.

description: Use a personal access token with domain read, create, update, and delete scopes for the operations you want DNSDeck to perform.
name: DigitalOcean

ttl.help: TTL must be at least 1 second. DigitalOcean may align TTLs for records in the same RRset.

description: Use a project-bound Hetzner Cloud API token. Read-only tokens can browse DNS; record and zone changes require a read-write token.
name: Hetzner

ttl.help: Automatic uses the zone default TTL. Explicit values must be between 60 and 2147483647 seconds.

description: Use a Linode API personal access token with domains read-only or read-write scope. DNS zones are served only while the account has an active Linode.
name: Akamai Cloud (Linode)

ttl.help: Record TTL is rounded up to the next Linode API value between 300 and 2419200 seconds.

description: Use a Vultr API key allowed to access DNS resources. Apex records use an empty API name and are shown as @ in DNSDeck.
name: Vultr

ttl.help: TTL is sent as whole seconds; Vultr's API does not publish a narrower numeric range.

credentials.help: The numeric ID shown after /a/ in the DNSimple application URL.
credentials.label: Account ID

description: Use a DNSimple account access token and numeric account ID. DNSDeck scopes record writes to DNSimple itself rather than propagating them to integrated zones.
name: DNSimple

ttl.help: DNSimple's OpenAPI contract accepts non-negative TTL values and defaults to 3600 seconds.

description: Use a scoped Gandi Personal Access Token. Legacy API-key authentication is deprecated and is not accepted by DNSDeck.
name: Gandi LiveDNS

ttl.help: LiveDNS accepts RRset TTL values from 300 through 2592000 seconds.

credentials.help: Only required for documented reseller subaccount access.
credentials.label: Shopper ID

description: Use a scoped GoDaddy Personal Access Token with domains.domain:read and domains.dns:update. Add domains.nameserver:update to change delegation; DNSDeck never uses domain purchase or cancellation endpoints.
name: GoDaddy

ttl.help: GoDaddy DNS records use TTL values from 600 seconds through one week.

description: Use a scoped Porkbun API key and secret. Enable API access for each domain you want DNSDeck to manage, and restrict the key by domain or source IP where possible.
name: Porkbun

ttl.help: Porkbun defaults omitted or zero TTLs to the account minimum, typically 600 seconds.

description: Use your Name.com username and Core API token. DNSDeck uses Core v1 rather than legacy v4; Name.com's current API documentation says accounts with two-step verification are not supported.
name: Name.com

ttl.help: Name.com Core API records use a minimum TTL of 300 seconds.

credentials.help: Namecheap requires the public IPv4 address making API requests. Add this address under Namecheap API Access → Whitelisted IPs, then enter the same address here. If your public IP changes, update it in both places.
credentials.label: Your public IPv4 address

credentials.help: Leave empty for production, or enter sandbox to use a separate Namecheap sandbox account.
credentials.label: API Environment

description: Use your Namecheap API username and key with an allowlisted public IPv4 address. Domains using external nameservers remain available for registrar delegation; host records require Namecheap DNS.
name: Namecheap

ttl.help: Namecheap host TTL values must be between 60 and 60000 seconds.

description: Use a Spaceship API key with domains:read and dnsrecords:read. Add domains:write for nameserver changes and dnsrecords:write for custom DNS record changes.
name: Spaceship

ttl.help: Spaceship DNS record TTLs must be between 60 and 3600 seconds.

credentials.help: Enter the complete key prefix and secret separated by a period.
credentials.label: API Key

description: Use an IONOS Hosting Developer API key in prefix.secret form. This connects to the Hosting DNS API; IONOS Cloud DNS is a separate product and credential system.
name: IONOS

ttl.help: DNSDeck uses IONOS's recommended 3600-second TTL and a conservative 300-second minimum.

credentials.help: Required only when creating a public DNS zone. Existing zones retain their own resource group.
credentials.label: Default Resource Group

description: Use a Microsoft Entra service principal scoped to the public DNS zones DNSDeck should manage. Subscription-wide discovery includes zones in every resource group; a default resource group is only needed when creating a zone.
name: Azure DNS

ttl.help: Azure DNS applies one TTL to an entire RRset, from 1 through 2147483647 seconds.

credentials.help: Use an unencrypted RSA private key in PKCS#8 or PKCS#1 PEM format.
credentials.label: Private API Key

credentials.help: Leave empty for oraclecloud.com. Enter the OCI realm domain only for a government or sovereign realm.
credentials.label: Realm Domain

description: Use an OCI API signing key and a compartment containing the public GLOBAL zones DNSDeck should manage. Private views and Traffic Management steering policies are separate OCI surfaces.
name: Oracle Cloud DNS

ttl.help: OCI accepts whole-second RRset TTLs; Oracle recommends values of at least 30 seconds.

description: Use a scoped deSEC API token. Domain creation and deletion require separate token permissions; RRset writes can be restricted by domain, subname, and type policies.
name: deSEC

ttl.help: deSEC caps TTLs at one day and enforces the minimum returned for each domain. DNSDeck applies that domain-specific minimum when writing.

credentials.help: For example, https://dns.example.com/api/v1. DNSDeck appends /api/v1 when omitted.
credentials.label: API Endpoint

credentials.help: Defaults to localhost, the standard PowerDNS server identifier.
credentials.label: Server ID

credentials.help: Optional authoritative nameserver added when DNSDeck creates a native zone.
credentials.label: Default Nameserver

description: Connect to a PowerDNS Authoritative HTTP API. Use HTTPS for remote servers; loopback HTTP is accepted for local development. Secondary zones are browsable but read-only.
name: PowerDNS Authoritative

ttl.help: PowerDNS accepts non-negative 32-bit TTL values and replaces an entire RRset in one zone PATCH.

description: Use a Scaleway secret key and Project ID with Domains and DNS v2beta1. DNSDeck manages existing zones, nameservers, and records; adding an external domain requires Scaleway's separate ownership-verification flow.
name: Scaleway Domains and DNS

ttl.help: Scaleway models TTL as an unsigned 32-bit number and versions every DNS record change.

description: Use an OVHcloud application key, application secret, and consumer key authorized for DNS zone, record, and domain nameserver paths. Zone ordering and service termination remain separate billing workflows.
name: OVHcloud DNS

ttl.help: OVHcloud accepts automatic TTL as 0; explicit TTLs must be at least 60 seconds.

description: Use a least-privilege IBM NS1 Connect API key secret. Primary zones and standard records are writable; secondary and linked zones remain read-only in DNSDeck.
name: IBM NS1 Connect

ttl.help: IBM NS1 Connect applies one non-negative TTL to a record and all of its answers.

description: Use an UltraDNS API-only username and password. Primary standard RRsets are writable; secondary, alias, pool, and directional records remain read-only in DNSDeck.
name: UltraDNS

ttl.help: UltraDNS accepts RRset TTLs from 0 through 2147483647 seconds.

description: Use an AWS access key with least-privilege Route 53 permissions. Nameserver changes also require Route 53 Domains access for domains registered in the same account.
name: Amazon Route 53

ttl.help: TTL must be between 1 and 2147483647 seconds.

credentials.help: Leave empty for a personal account.
credentials.label: Team ID

description: Use a Vercel access token with domain permissions. Team ID is optional for a personal account and scopes requests when supplied.
name: Vercel

ttl.help: TTL must be at least 60 seconds.

description: Use a service account JSON key with DNS Administrator permissions and the project that owns the managed zones. Cloud Domains nameserver changes require domains.registrations.configureDns.
name: Google Cloud DNS

ttl.help: TTL must be between 1 and 2147483647 seconds.
